meta.title: The Shop That Closes at Noon
meta.skill_frame: Use facts in the passage to work out something it does not say directly.

reader.who: Older students who read at about a fourth-grade level.
reader.why_this_level: The load is two links: the delivery needs the shop floor, and counting needs the aisles empty. Measured FK 5.9-7.2 on the 2 parts (Flesch-Kincaid, approximate syllable count). The load sits inside the grade 4-5 band and rises across the stage.
reader.tone: Adult subject. Plain sentences. The lesson must not make the reader feel small.

source.attribution: Original text drafted for inference 4.2, sequence 5. No external work.
source.survey: Written to the stage: everyday subject, stated facts, links held apart.
source.avoided: No named real places or people. No figures that could go stale.

session.difficulty_basis: Clue distance and number of links, climbing one knob per sequence.

script_overrides.near_copy_2: Say it in your own words. One sentence is enough.

passage.part_1: The hardware store on Mill Street closes at noon every Wednesday, and the sign on the door has said so for years. On other days the store stays open until six. A customer who came on a Wednesday afternoon found the door locked and the lights off. The owner was not away, and the shelves were not empty.
passage.part_2: Wednesday afternoon is when the delivery truck arrives. The store has one narrow back door and no loading bay. Boxes have to be carried through the shop floor and counted against the invoice as they come in. With customers in the aisles that counting cannot be done. The owner closes for the afternoon, takes the delivery, and restocks before Thursday.

items.prompt: When does the store close early?

tutor_only.correct_reason: The first sentence gives the closing time.
tutor_only.tell: It closes at noon on Wednesdays and stays open until six on other days.

if_they_say.when: the student says it is closed for the day
if_they_say.ask: It closes at noon and reopens Thursday. Which day does that happen?

items.prompt: The customer found the door locked and the lights off. What does that suggest?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. The closing was planned, not an accident.
tutor_only.correct_reason: A shop that has gone dark and locked up is not having a slow afternoon. The sign and the years of practice agree.
tutor_only.tell: Lights off and a locked door look like a plan. A shop in trouble would be open.
help: Look at what a shop looks like when it shuts down for a reason.
Then look at what the sign has said for years.
tutor_only.core_idea: The shop was closed on purpose, as it is every Wednesday.

if_they_say.when: the student says the store went out of business
if_they_say.ask: The shelves were not empty. What does the sign on the door say?

items.prompt: Why close the store instead of counting the delivery with customers there?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. The counting cannot be done with customers in the aisles.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The passage says boxes come through the shop floor and are counted against the invoice, which cannot happen in a busy aisle.
tutor_only.tell: The boxes have to pass through the shop. Counting them while serving customers does not work.
help: Find the sentence about customers in the aisles.
Look at what the counting needs.
tutor_only.core_idea: The delivery has to be counted as it comes in, and that needs the aisles clear.
accept_ideas: the counting needs an empty shop
you cannot count with customers there

if_they_say.when: the student says the owner wanted a day off
if_they_say.ask: The passage says the owner was not away. What does the delivery need?

items.prompt: Why does the narrow back door matter?

tutor_only.confirm: Yes. Boxes have to come through the shop floor.
tutor_only.correct_reason: Without a loading bay the delivery must cross the shop, which is why customers and counting conflict.
tutor_only.tell: A wide back door would let boxes bypass the shop. This one does not, so the boxes go through the aisles.
help: Find the sentence about the back door.
Look at where the boxes have to go after that door.
tutor_only.core_idea: It forces every box through the shop floor.
accept_ideas: the boxes come through the shop
the boxes go through the aisles
it makes the delivery cross the shop

if_they_say.when: the student says the door is hard to open
if_they_say.ask: The problem is the route the boxes take. Where do they end up?

items.prompt: Why Wednesday and not another afternoon?

tutor_only.confirm: Right. That is when the delivery truck comes.
tutor_only.correct_reason: The closing exists to receive the delivery, and the delivery arrives on Wednesday afternoon.
tutor_only.tell: The shop closes when the delivery comes. Move the delivery and the closing would move with it.
help: Find the sentence that says when the truck arrives.
tutor_only.core_idea: Because Wednesday afternoon is when the delivery truck arrives.
accept_ideas: that is when the truck comes

if_they_say.when: the student says Wednesday is quiet
if_they_say.ask: Quietness is not mentioned. What does the passage say happens on Wednesday afternoon?

advance.next_means: The first lesson in the next inference stage.
advance.student_line: You have the move. The next reading is another lesson on this skill.

retry.student_line: The next reading is another lesson on this skill in this stage.
